source.title: Towards Universality: Studying Mechanistic Similarity Across Language Model Architectures
source.authors: Junxuan Wang; Xu-Yang Ge; Wentao Shu; Qiong Tang; Yunhua Zhou; Zheng-Fu He; Xi-Peng Qiu

page_placements.theme: Universality and reproducibility of units across seeds, architectures, dictionary fits and paraphrased inputs

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and tables are flattened in the extraction, but the reported results used here are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares feature similarity across language-model architectures using SAE features and correlation metrics, a different measurement from the claimed audit of neuron-pole job counts.
record.gate_note: The study measures cross-model activation-feature similarity, not the fraction of neuron poles with one or two jobs or the share that remains unexplained. Its neuron-correlation baseline is also not a direct test of single-job interpretability. A figure in the main text reports distributions, but the reported averages and thresholds are available in text. The cited 1%–5% neuron result and cited prior circuit findings are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It matches SAE features (not neurons) across Pythia-160M, Mamba-130M and RWKV-169M by activation correlation (MPPC). It never reports what share of neurons or neuron poles have one main job, two related jobs, or no explanation. The neuron baseline (r4) measures cross-architecture neuron matching, not single-job interpretability. The GPT-4o complexity and monosemanticity scores, done in the style of Bills et al., are applied to SAE features and reported only as MPPC distributions. The paper cites Bills et al. and polysemanticity as motivation for using SAEs, but does not test the claim. The reader's 'tests/T2' for V2 is wrong: V2 concerns shares of interpretable neurons across models, while this study measures cross-model feature similarity, a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that most SAE features are similar across Pythia and Mamba, and that the result carries over to RWKV. They add that MPPC is affected by feature complexity, which they cancel by subtracting the seed skyline. The record omits two further conclusions: Mamba's induction circuit is structurally analogous to the Transformer one, and Mamba shows an 'Off-by-One' motif, writing a token's information into the SSM state at the next position.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE decomposition and maximum pairwise activation correlation across models, rather than auditing neuron-pole explanations against held-out activations. Tests relatively small models, not Qwen3-32B. The circuit analysis uses path patching, not the claimed attribution-graph procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity depends on architecture pair and matching direction: Pythia-to-Mamba average MPPC is 0.74 versus Mamba-to-Pythia 0.78; Pythia-to-RWKV is 0.65. The paper also reports that feature complexity affects MPPC.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features match across Transformer, Mamba and RWKV (mean MPPC 0.74, 0.78 reverse, 0.65 for RWKV). Similarity is just below same-architecture seed skylines (0.76, 0.81). More than 30% of Pythia features have MPPC above 0.95.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-autoencoder features in small language models are largely shared across architectures (Transformer, Mamba, RWKV).

fits_no_version.finding: Raw neuron activations barely match across architectures (mean MPPC 0.30), unlike the 1–5% universal neurons Gurnee et al. found across Transformer seeds (a cited result).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron bases are not comparable across language-model architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Features with cross-architecture MPPC below about 0.2 are mostly rated non-monosemantic and look uninterpretable on manual inspection. Higher-MPPC features are mostly simple single-token features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model feature matching tracks SAE feature interpretability and complexity.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR); the supplied paper text is marked “Preprint. Under Review.”
record.problems: The studied models are small (Pythia-160M, Mamba-130M, and RWKV-169M). Similarity is assessed using SAE features and MPPC, not an independent test of neuron explanations or the share of poles with a single job. The paper notes that SAEs may miss true features or capture combinations of them. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported averages.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested feature-similarity comparisons. The induction-circuit path-patching results are not included because they do not measure neuron-pole job shares or the cross-model feature-similarity measure in V2.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job shares.
No neuron job-share measurement in any model. Models are small (130M–169M), and there are no mixture-of-experts or trillion-parameter models.
No vision models and no InceptionV1 neurons.
No study of how architecture or tools affect neuron interpretability rates.
No neuron-based attribution graphs. The circuit work uses path patching on Mamba induction and IOI.
No held-out prediction test of neuron explanations.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations. GPT-4o rates complexity and consistency of SAE features from top-10 activating examples only.

missing.what: Distribution of MPPC by GPT-4o monosemanticity score for SAE features, with a boundary near MPPC 0.2. This concerns SAE features, not neurons, so it is relevant only under fits_no_version.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked SAE feature similarity to V2, but V2 is about the share of interpretable neurons across models, which this study never measures. All rows are relinked to none and no verdicts are given. The study is an ICLR submission (marked 'Preprint. Under Review'). The cited Gurnee 1–5% result is not this study's own result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or report shares with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood jobs.

Tests cross-architecture feature similarity in Pythia-160M with Mamba-130M and RWKV-169M, not neuron-pole job shares. Does not test dense versus mixture-of-experts models or models up to trillions of parameters.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not study vision models, late-layer neuron interpretability rates, or the stated architecture/tool estimates.
Does not test attribution graphs built from a large model’s own neurons, compare against a trained replacement model, or report reconstruction error.
Does not test whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict held-out neuron activations.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

relation.reason: The 2024 paper does not test the claim and does not engage with it. Its only neuron-interpretability content is one related-work line that neurons are polysemantic (citing Elhage et al.), used to motivate SAEs. Its neuron baseline is about matching neurons across models, not about interpretability. So 'discusses' overstates it, and cites_only is the nearest label.

tranche.reason: Matches SAE features and raw activations across architectures. Never measures what share of neurons have one main job or are interpretable, so it neither tests nor uses any version.

source_check.notes: Measures cross-architecture SAE feature similarity (MPPC) for Pythia-160M, Mamba-130M and RWKV-169M, so it bears on no version. r7/r8 repeat r2/r3's Pythia-only skylines from Figure 11a. Reverse 0.78 exceeds the 0.76 model-seed skyline, and RWKV's 0.65 is 0.11 below it. The GPT-4o scoring prompts in Appendix E are method prompts, not instructions to a reader.

statements.correction: Pythia to Mamba SAE MPPC 0.74, against 0.76 (model-seed skyline) and 0.81 (SAE-seed skyline). The paper says it 'slightly falls short of skylines'. Reverse, Mamba to Pythia: 0.78, above the model-seed skyline (0.76 forward, 0.75 reverse) and below 0.81. Authors attribute this mainly to Mamba having more low-level features. Pythia to RWKV: 0.65, against the same 0.76 and 0.81. Authors call it slightly lower than Mamba. Neuron baseline (Pythia MLP neurons vs Mamba post-SiLU activations): 0.30, 'almost exhibits zero sign of similarity'.
statements.problem: All numbers are in the text. But 'just below same-architecture seed skylines' fits only the forward Pythia-to-Mamba 0.74. The reverse Mamba-to-Pythia 0.78 is above the 0.76 model-seed skyline (and above its reverse counterpart, 0.75). Pythia-to-RWKV 0.65 is 0.11 below 0.76, not just below.
